answer: Superlinear bond sizing resists sybils: the Nth identity funded from one source must lock a bond that grows with N, so the second seat costs more than the first and the tenth far more. A vault bankrolling a swarm pays steeply for scale while one honest agent posts a single flat bond. A falcon-eyed check ties bonds to common funding roots, so a juniper-thick farm cannot cheaply multiply when each added head is priced above the last. Capital, not headcount, bounds influence.
